newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Dying man seeks first Irish divorce.
newsitem.headline: Dying man seeks first Irish divorce.

text.p: A dying man tried on Wednesday to become the first recipient of an Irish divorce since it was legalised in a referendum in 1995.
The unnamed man applied to the Dublin high court to be granted a divorce by virtue of its approval by a tiny majority in a plebiscite in November 1995.
A law enabling divorce for the first time in the overwhelmingly Roman Catholic Irish republic is not due to take effect until the end of next month.
So the man, who says he is terminally ill, wants divorce granted him under constitutional guarantees of his rights.
The court heard his plea in camera after the man asked the judge that the media be kept out of the proceedings.
The man, in his 50s, says he has only a short time to live and has been separated from his wife for many years and wants to marry the woman with whom he has been living before he dies.
Divorce was legalised in Ireland after a bitterly contested referendum which was approved by a 0.56 percent majority, the narrowest majority in the history of the Irish state.
